summary: With every finding and correction recorded, this turn chased one more suspicion of the same family as the log-read paths replication and commit decisions depend on: that the log cache could serve an entry value the log store no longer agrees with, since the cache keeps the caller's pointers and a producer mutating a Log after storing it would leave the two views different. The answer is a scoped negative, and I recorded it as one rather than inflating it. Two independent grounds refute it for in-tree producers. The read path is conservative: a ring slot is returned only when its index matches the requested one, otherwise the request falls through to the store, and DeleteRange clears the whole ring before the store deletes, so no truncated suffix can be served from the cache. And the two views hold the same objects: StoreLogs caches the pointers it was handed while the in-memory store keeps those same pointers, so a mutation would move both together rather than separate them. On the producer side, each non-test call site fills the entry before storing it and only reads it afterwards, the leader assigning index, term and timestamp before StoreLogs, the follower storing decoded entries and then reading them, and bootstrap writing one entry and returning. The residual hazard is real but external and narrower than the suspicion: a caller that hands a Log to a copying store such as a serializing disk store and then mutates that same Log would have the cache serve the mutated object while the durable copy kept the original. I stated that boundary for callers instead of dressing it up as a defect, recorded the behaviour with its conditions and the six source ranges, and marked the suspicion refuted within its stated scope. No execution was spent, which is right for a claim about which code paths mutate what. The six witnessed findings, the reproduced regression with its causal control, and the two knowledge corrections remain recorded and unaffected.
